batch_notes: (1) Two recurring shapes sit between the rubric's categories: (a) test-written protocol encoders / token grammars that emit (input, expected) pairs by construction (x-input and ultraviolet decoders, x-ansi's ECMA-48 token grammar) - classified model-oracle when the encoder is a substantive spec model, spec-postcondition when the construction is trivial (paste markers, one-cluster keys); (b) round trips whose inverse is a test-written decoder (ultraviolet StylesRoundTripThroughSGR, LinesRenderWhatTheyHold) - classified model-oracle by analogy with the external-tool tie-break. (2) uniseg's oracle is a Python UAX #29 reference written by the harness and validated against the UCD test files; classified model-oracle although it runs as a child process, since the rubric's 'another language's implementation' reads as a pre-existing one - worth a rubric clarification. (3) The ultraviolet and x-input READMEs carry an explicit per-property Gates column naming bug ids, so attribution there is mostly explicit; bugs with no gate (ultraviolet/2,8,10,13,33; x-input/5,7,8; x-ansi/2,3,4,16,22; uuid/1,3) look found by code reading, by a deterministic boundary example, or inherited from a sibling package (ultraviolet re-pins x-input bugs; x-ansi/22 surfaced while writing ultraviolet's encoders). (4) Data quirk: several bug records have property=null while a property's bugs_direct lists them (uniseg/1,2 on Widths; x-ansi/6,7 on Truncate; ultraviolet/22,26,27,32); bugs_direct seems derived from mentioned_by/gates rather than from the record's test field. (5) No property in this batch is a narrowed pin; all 80 pins are example tests. (6) Notable: the x/vt emulator differential found two renderer bugs at low rates (7% of frames, 1 in 20000 sequences); KeystrokesMatchTheirKeys (MatchString(Keystroke())) is a cheap API-ergonomics property that gated six bugs; the Go layout solver is checked against the Rust original (ratatui) it translates. (7) x-ansi's two wrap properties are invariant-only (style/content preservation plus width) because the algorithm is unspecified, and they gate seven bugs between them - a case where a weak spec still finds many bugs.
